findings.current: Only thirty-two seats were prepared for the grand council. That had been true a hundred years ago, and it was still true now.
findings.defect: This contradicts the surrounding seat count: thirty-one seats are occupied and two are empty, so thirty-three seats have been prepared today.
findings.rationale: The replacement preserves the traditional count while allowing today’s unexplained extra seat to produce the stated total of two empty seats.
findings.replacement: For the past hundred years, only thirty-two seats had been prepared for the grand council.

findings.current: “For the Nanman warriors who fell victim to the hands……no, the slime and webs of those bastards I could tear to pieces and still not feel satisfied.”
findings.defect: The self-correction never closes grammatically, leaving “those bastards” attached to both the victims and the following clause.
findings.rationale: This completes the hand-to-slime-and-webs joke and restores a clear, natural declaration of vengeance without changing the meaning.
findings.replacement: “For the Nanman warriors who fell victim to the hands… no, the slime and webs of those bastards. Even tearing them to pieces wouldn’t satisfy me.”
findings.source: Chapter 640, Jin explaining why he killed the Thousand-Year Spider

findings.current: The Wraith of Ailao Mountain has no intention of harming us.
findings.defect: The epithet drifts from the established form “Ailao Mountain’s Wraith.”
findings.rationale: Using the established epithet consistently prevents the same entity from appearing to have two translated names.
findings.replacement: Ailao Mountain’s Wraith has no intention of harming us.
